requirement: A forged or altered packet is rejected before its contents are used
tests: secure_link/test/test_host.c::open: 1-bit change in ciphertext rejected;secure_link/test/test_host.c::open: edited counter rejected (MIC covers the header);secure_link/test/test_host.c::open: wrong key rejected (MIC), counter unchanged;secure_link/test/test_host.c::AES-128 FIPS-197 Appendix C.1;secure_link/test/test_host.c::RFC 4493
note: The 4-byte tag allows a blind guess with probability 2^-32 per attempt (the same trade-off as LoRaWAN)

requirement: A captured packet cannot be replayed, and the counter never goes backwards across reboots or power cuts
tests: secure_link/test/test_host.c::open: replayed packet rejected;secure_link/test/test_fcnt.c::after power cut + reboot: resumes above every value used;secure_link/test/test_fcnt.c::20 reboots in a row: counter never repeats or goes backwards
note: After a receiver reboot up to 100 genuine packets can be rejected (the replay floor moves in steps of 100)

requirement: The reading is not sent in plain text, and the keystream is the one the standard defines
tests: secure_link/test/test_host.c::seal: payload is not sent in plain text;secure_link/test/test_host.c::Known-answer test for the AES-CTR keystream
note: Device id, counter, length and timing stay visible

requirement: The keystream is never reused after a reset
tests: secure_link/test/test_fcnt.c::reboot: first counter after reset is above every value used;secure_link/test/test_fcnt.c::erased EEPROM (all zeros) is treated as fresh
note: If the counter state is lost (for example the EEPROM erased with a debugger) keystreams can repeat; the debug port is locked

requirement: Jamming or forged-frame flooding is not prevented
note: Physical layer; the EU 1 % duty cycle limits only the node's own transmissions. Each forged frame costs the receiver one MIC check

requirement: A modified application, an unsigned image, an image signed with another key, or a re-hashed image is refused at boot
tests: bootloader/test/test_image.c::signed with the trusted key: accepted;bootloader/test/test_image.c::unsigned image (no --key): rejected, signature;bootloader/test/test_image.c::signed with a different key: rejected, signature;bootloader/test/test_image.c::bit flipped after signing: rejected, hash;bootloader/test/test_image.c::attacker bumps the version and fixes the hash: rejected, signature;bootloader/test/test_image.c::1 bit flipped in the stored signature: rejected;bootloader/test/test_ecdsa.c::1 bit flipped in s: rejected
note: The threat model cites refusal on hardware; there is no log file for it in the repository

requirement: A correctly signed older image is refused, and the stored minimum version survives a power cut or a corrupted copy
tests: bootloader/test/test_update.c::update older than the minimum version: rejected (rollback), slot A untouched;bootloader/test/test_rollback.c::one corrupted copy: the other copy still holds 2.0.0;bootloader/test/test_rollback.c::next boot repairs the corrupted copy A;bootloader/test/test_rollback.c::power cut mid-write is reported
note: Compares version numbers, not contents. The threat model cites refusal on hardware; there is no log file for it in the repository

requirement: A power cut at any point of an update leaves a complete valid image, and the next boot finishes the job
tests: bootloader/test/test_update.c::power cut at every few operations of the copy;bootloader/test/test_update.c::A already equals B: only slot B is cleared (1 operation)
note: The 1,682 cut points are simulated; a real USB power cut is cited in the threat model with no log file in the repository

requirement: Weakened bootloader protection is detected at boot and the chip refuses to start
tests: bootloader/test/test_ob_check.c::sector 0 missing;bootloader/test/test_ob_check.c::WPRMOD=1 (bits mean PCROP);bootloader/test/test_ob_check.c::BFB2=1 (boot from bank 2);bootloader/test/test_ob_check.c::everything wrong at level 0
note: Software can rewrite the option bytes, so removal is only noticed at the next reset

requirement: Read-out protection Level 1 is required, and Level 2 is recognised and never set
tests: bootloader/test/test_ob_check.c::RDP 0xCC = level 2;bootloader/test/test_ob_check.c::RDP 0x55 = level 1 (any other value);bootloader/test/test_ob_check.c::production target (WRP 0-5, level 1)
note: Level 1 is not designed to resist fault injection; keys sit in internal flash

requirement: A compromised application can write the EEPROM records and the option bytes
note: No privilege separation on this Cortex-M0+; removal of protection is caught at the next boot

requirement: The private signing key is kept off the device and in a protected backup
note: The key sits in a git-ignored folder with an AES-256 gpg backup that was restore-tested; nothing in the repository can check that, and a compromised laptop means full signing power

requirement: A false sensor reading that is correctly authenticated is not prevented
note: The link protects the packet, not the truth of the measurement

requirement: Rejected updates and failed boots are recorded in a persistent log
note: Messages go to the UART only; nothing is stored

requirement: A slow brown-out during a flash write is handled
note: Brown-out reset is off (factory setting); production should enable it

requirement: Anything that weakens the protection stops the device from booting (it fails closed)
note: Deliberate: option-byte writing code is one bug from an unprogrammable chip; the availability cost is accepted

requirement: The SHA-256 and ECDSA code agree with published test vectors
tests: bootloader/test/test_sha256.c::abcdbcdecdefdefgefghfghighijhijkijkljklmklmnlmnomnopnopq;bootloader/test/test_sha256.c::SHA-256 in irregular pieces == one call;bootloader/test/test_ecdsa.c::RFC 6979 public key is a valid P-256 point;bootloader/test/test_ecdsa.c::all-zero signature (unsigned image): rejected
note: No independent review and no side-channel evaluation
